text.tspan: gives exam scores for a sample of 5 students in a morning class,
and exam scores for a sample of 5 students in an evening class. Use STAT-Utility to find the mean, median,
range, variance, and standard deviation for each sample.
These are samples, so the sample variance and sample standard deviation that STAT-Utility gives
by default are what we need. First, type the data into two columns named “Morning Class” and
“Evening Class.” Select Descriptive Statistics → Basic Statistics and check both columns under
“Columns to include.” Under “Statistics to show,” also check “Range (max − min).” Then click
As we saw in example 1, the mean and median of each class is 82. The range of the morning class
was 25 while the range of the evening class was smaller at 20. But we also noted that the morning
class had three scores very close together around the mean. We suggested that the morning class
was more consistent, and that can be seen in the slightly smaller standard deviation. The standard
deviation for the morning class is 8.9, and the standard deviation for the evening class is 9.1, both
rounded to one decimal place (we usually round standard deviation to one or two more decimal
places than the original data). That means that the morning class grades were slightly more
